C004F_4_dirichlet_form.derivation: Standard graph identity f^T L g = (1/2) sum_ij A_ij(f_i-f_j)(g_i-g_j), combined with <f,-Qg>_mu = (1/(2|E_k|)) f^T L g (from Q=-D^{-1}L and pi_i/d_i=1/(2|E_k|)).

C004F_4_dirichlet_form.positivity: E_k(f,f) = (1/(2E)) f^T L f >= 0 (L is PSD, proven throughout this project)
C004F_4_dirichlet_form.kernel: ker(E_k) = span{1} -- PROVEN: E_k(f,f)=0 iff Lf=0 iff f is constant (G connected)
C004F_4_dirichlet_form.corollary: Since E_k(f,g)=<f,-Qg>_mu is manifestly symmetric in f,g (built from (f_i-f_j)(g_i-g_j)), Q is SELF-ADJOINT w.r.t. <.,.>_mu -- this proves THEOREM C-004F.2 (weighted reversibility) as a direct corollary, without a separate argument.

entropy_production_consequence_section_1.question: Does F[P||P_ss] yield sigma=-dF/dt>=0 directly from the recovered generator Q*, without choosing P(0) or t?
entropy_production_consequence_section_1.answer: YES, as an INEQUALITY (not a specific number). Standard Lyapunov-function argument for reversible Markov generators: dF/dt = sum_i(Q*P)_i log(P_i/pi_i) [using conservation, proven C-004F.3], which symmetrizes via detailed balance [proven C-004F.3] into a sum of terms of the form -(1/2)pi_i Q_ij(a-b)(log a - log b) with a=P_j/pi_j, b=P_i/pi_i, each term <=0 by the elementary inequality (a-b)(log a-log b)>=0 for a,b>0. Hence dF/dt<=0 always, i.e. sigma=-dF/dt>=0, for ANY trajectory -- this requires ONLY detailed balance + conservation (both now concretely proven for Q*, not merely asserted abstractly as in BRIDGE B-006), NOT a choice of P(0) or evaluation time.
entropy_production_consequence_section_1.numerical_sanity_check: Confirmed sigma>=0 numerically across 12 sampled (P(0),t) combinations (4 random P(0), 3 times each) for every shell G0-G4; see c004f_entropy_consequence.json. No sample or trajectory choice is treated as canonical -- this is a sanity check of the algebra, not a determination of sigma_k's value.
